title: Kurt Burris: OU Center and 1954 Heisman Runner-Up
question: Which Oklahoma center finished second in the 1954 Heisman Trophy voting?
answer: Kurt Burris, a consensus All-American center, finished second to Wisconsin's Alan Ameche in the 1954 Heisman voting. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2000.
summary: Kurt Burris, Oklahoma's center and linebacker from 1951 to 1954, was a consensus All-American and the 1954 Heisman runner-up. Here is his story.
body: Kurt Burris was a center at Oklahoma from 1951 to 1954, back when one-platoon football meant a center also played linebacker. He grew up in Muskogee, and the College Football Hall of Fame credits him with a four-year stretch in which the Sooners went 35-4-2.

His best season was 1954. Burris was a consensus All-American at center, and the Helms Foundation named him its national player of the year. He also finished second in that year's Heisman Trophy voting, behind Wisconsin's Alan Ameche, which is remarkable company for a man who snapped the ball and tackled for a living.

He was drafted in the first round of the 1955 NFL draft by the Cleveland Browns, but he signed with the Edmonton Eskimos of the Canadian league instead. He played in the CFL until a knee injury ended his career after the 1960 season, then built a career in the oil drilling business in Canada and the American West.

Burris died in 1999, and the National Football Foundation inducted him into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2000. Anyone who wants to understand why those early-1950s Oklahoma teams were so hard to beat can start with the man in the middle of the line.
